questions.q: According to this lesson, when should you sketch the architecture diagram relative to opening a cloud console?
options: It doesn't matter, since diagrams have no effect on deployment quality
Only after a serious outage has already occurred
After the environment is fully deployed and already handling real traffic
Before — the diagram comes together on paper before any of it comes together in a console
questions.explain: The lesson's core point is that the sketch forces you to work through connections before committing real resources.

questions.q: What three things does a real architecture diagram need to show, per this lesson?
options: The exact dollar cost of every resource, with nothing about how they connect
Network layout, compute tiers, and data flow
A single undifferentiated box labeled "the app"
Only the company logo and project name
questions.explain: The lesson calls a diagram missing any of these three 'a box with an arrow,' not a real architecture diagram.

questions.q: Why does the lesson say data flow is the piece most likely to reveal a real design problem?
options: It only matters for billing reports, not for system design
Data flow is identical for every workload, so it never reveals anything new
Data flow has no connection to how tiers actually interact
It shows how a request actually moves through the system, exposing a tier with access it shouldn't have or a bottleneck dependency
questions.explain: Tracing the request path is what surfaces problems like an inappropriate direct access path or a dependency bottleneck.

questions.q: Why is catching a design mistake on paper cheaper than catching it after deployment, according to this lesson?
options: Cloud providers automatically fix architecture mistakes once they're deployed
Paper mistakes are free because diagrams aren't reviewed by anyone else
There's no real cost difference between the two situations
A paper mistake costs a conversation and an eraser mark, while the same mistake found after deployment can mean tearing down and rebuilding live infrastructure
questions.explain: The whole point of diagramming first is moving discovery of a problem to the cheapest possible moment.

questions.q: What does this lesson say should happen to the architecture diagram after the environment is actually built?
options: It should be deleted immediately, since its only purpose was the initial planning meeting
It should be kept and updated, becoming the first page of real documentation for the environment
It should be replaced entirely by a generic template with no project-specific detail
It should be printed and never referenced again
questions.explain: The lesson treats the diagram as a living artifact that later documentation and handoff work builds directly on.
